decontamination_notes: cii-v2 candidate #5 under the hard-band gate (best model <=2/3). sqlglot #8063 (fixes #8035, merged 2026-08-10, flagged as a breaking parser change): ->, ->>, #>, #>> and ? were parsed via COLUMN_OPERATORS as tight-binding accessors instead of Postgres's actual binary-operator tier (below +/-, level with ||, left-associative), corrupting adjacent casts, subscripts and arithmetic. Convention-heavy: the correct behavior is defined by Postgres's operator table, interacts with the parser's precedence-climbing structure, and must change for postgres+duckdb while leaving lambda-arrow dialects untouched. GRADING SUBTLETY solved during the build and worth keeping for future parser tasks: the upstream diff changes both BINDING (semantics) and RENDERING (the generator now emits -> instead of JSON_EXTRACT_PATH). To grade semantics only, every assertion compares parse-tree STRUCTURE: repr() of the tree with grouping Paren nodes stripped, asserting tree(X) == tree(X-with-explicit-parens) and != tree(wrong-reading). Two earlier comparison schemes were rejected as unsound: raw canonical SQL (parens render, so the explicit reading never equals the bare one) and paren-stripped canonical SQL (the generator re-renders distinct bindings to identical text, collapsing the comparison). Differentially probed 21 corners at base vs gold in-image: 13 diverge; the 4 fail_to_pass tests cover cast-binds-to-operand (all three text operators), arithmetic-binds-tighter, subscript-binds-to-operand, and duckdb sharing the tier. Left-associativity of chained extractions already held at base (verified) and is a GUARD, not f2p, alongside lambda-dialect preservation, ordinary precedence, paren round-trips, the ? operator, and postgres->duckdb transpilation. Per the v2 charter: no fix-location hints; the issue states Postgres's documented precedence facts and the observable mis-bindings only.
